resale_co.name: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (Certificate of Change in Ownership / Change in Occupancy), Borough Code Chapter 112
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Magnolia Construction Office (building inspector or housing inspector)
requirements: Home must meet the property maintenance standards the Borough adopted (BOCA National Property Maintenance Code, 1993) and all Borough ordinances
Hard-wired, interconnected smoke detectors with battery backup on or near the ceiling of each level
Battery smoke detectors in each bedroom or sleeping area
Smoke detectors must be certified by the fire official or other authorized person before the certificate is issued
Any repairs needed for the certificate are the current owner's responsibility, even if the problem was caused by a previous owner

Under Ordinance 12-2026 (adopted Sept 2, 2026) the owner stays responsible until the certificate is issued, no matter what the sale contract, settlement or escrow agreement says; each day of violation after notice is a separate offense

fees.label: Certificate of Continued Occupancy inspection when a home is sold (Borough page; same as Code 15.112-11 "Change of property ownership, Residential")
fees.quote: turn it into the Construction Office with the $75.00 fee

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Certificate of Continued Occupancy Application (linked from the Borough's "Certificate of Change in Occupancy" page, with an inspection checklist) and turn it in to the Construction Office, 438 W. Evesham Ave, Magnolia, with the $75.00 fee. An inspector will contact you to schedule. The owner or the owner's agent must apply.

resale_co.notes: Re-checked October 20, 2026. The live magnolia-nj.org site is still behind a Cloudflare check (HTTP 403), and the Internet Archive has no capture newer than January 2026, so the Borough page is cited from the January 11, 2026 capture. The Borough code on Municode was read this round (Chapter 112, Certificates of Occupancy): a certificate is required before occupancy after a change of ownership, issued by the building or housing inspector, and Code 15.112-11 A(1) sets $75.00 for a residential change of property ownership, the same fee the Borough page quotes (not listed twice). Code 15.112-2 says the Borough CO is issued only after the fire official or other authorized person certifies the smoke detectors. Code 15.112-11 C: if violations are not fixed after the first inspection and one reinspection, or the applicant misses the reinspection, the inspector may charge a reinspection fee equal to a new application. The Code also lists $150.00 for a "Certificate of continued occupancy, UCC permits may be required" and $50.00 per extension of a temporary CO. Failure to comply: fine up to $500.00 per day (15.112-12). Ordinance 12-2026 (adopted Sept 2, 2026) keeps the owner responsible until the certificate issues; it was read last round and not re-read. The application is an Adobe cloud link and the checklist file was not archived, so neither was read. Construction Office email for inspections: inspections@magnolia-nj.org (January 2026 capture of the Inspections page).

fire_cert.notes: The NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety is Magnolia's fire code enforcing agency ('S' = State in the July 2026 LEA Registry; Fire Official Louis Kilmer, NJ Div Fire Safety). On the DCA 'State Enforced Towns' list (revised 7/17/2026) Magnolia has NO 'SC' (Smoke Certs) mark, while nearby Stratford and Woodlynne do, and the DCA fire directory lists the smoke detector compliance contact as the Magnolia Borough Construction Office, 438 West Evesham Ave, (856) 783-1520. So the smoke/CO certificate appears to be handled locally by the Borough, not by DCA, which is why the state $45 / $90 / $161 fees are not recorded here. The directory's fire official block for Magnolia also notes an 'SSA with Barrington Boro' (the same note appears for Hi-Nella and Lawnside, which use Barrington's Regional Fire Prevention Alliance), but the Alliance's own page does not list Magnolia. Lawnside's code still lists Magnolia as an Alliance member, which looks out of date. Last round, Magnolia Code Chapter 142 Article II (Ord. 2018-05, Alliance-era fees $56 / $64 / $96 / $161) was found on Municode; it was not re-read this round and those amounts are not recorded as current. Code 15.112-2 ties the Borough CO to a smoke detector certification, so the smoke check may be part of the $75.00 Borough inspection. No fee or form for a separate certificate was found.
